messages:
samir: Heads-up — I found a case where a streaming request that falls back from Dedicated -> Hosted + then triggers a server-side toolcall appears to be double-billed. repro below.
ashley: ugh. can you paste the logs and request ids? :grimacing:
samir: minimal repro steps:
- send streaming chat to dedicated (route A)
- router hits capacity and falls back to hosted (route B) with a new worker
- stream sends first N chunks, model issues toolcall (external tool webhook) and we truncate/commit the stream
- hosted path retries the final commit (idempotency token mismatch) and both the initial and retried commits generate CHARGE events
logs:
```
req=rc-11f2 route=A->B fallback=true idempotency=none
stream_chunk seq=0 size=128
stream_chunk seq=1 size=256
toolcall invoke id=tc-77 request_id=rc-11f2 tool=kb-annotate
commit attempt=1 charge_event id=chg-900 tokens=384
commit attempt=2 idempotency_token_missing charge_event id=chg-901 tokens=384
```
ashley: that looks like two commits for the same logical session. does router create a new billing session on fallback?
jordan: yes currently we create a new reservation when we forward to a new pool, since we treat it like a fresh subrequest. that makes sense for routing isolation but breaks accounting if the original stream had outstanding reserved tokens.
kai: also worth noting toolcalls complicate things because the model host can trigger a downstream commit before the client sees final stream end. our current billing hook is 'on-commit' and it doesn't reconcile reservation ids across pools.
samir: proposal: introduce a reservation_id propagated with the request across routes + require commit to include reservation_id. billing logic should dedupe by reservation_id + terminal_nonce. pseudocode:
```
// router forwards fallback
if (request.reservation_id) {
  forward.metadata.reservation_id = request.reservation_id
} else {
  forward.metadata.reservation_id = billing.reserve(request.client, est_tokens)
}
// on commit
if (billing.commit(reservation_id, terminal_nonce)) {
  emit_charge(reservation_id, committed_tokens)
} else {
  ignore_duplicate()
}
```
kai: +1 but also need idempotency for toolcall-triggered commits. tool servers must echo the reservation_id back on callback.
jordan: console/telemetry changes we should add:
- reserved_tokens and committed_tokens per request in the trace
- a new event `partial_stream_commit` for toolcall-initiated truncates
- a reconciliation gauge: `uncommitted_reserved_tokens{route}`
ashley: UX idea: show a small badge when a request used fallback routing and link to the commit trace so support can see if duplicate charges happened.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026 — investigate retry-related double billing (assigned @billing-team)
samir: edgecases: what about KV-cache eviction causing a later recompute/rollback and extra tokens? reservation should cover speculative work and only be consumed on final commit. eviction-triggered recompute must reuse same reservation if within reservation_ttl or else refund/credit on reconciliation.
kai: implementation tasks:
- [ ] propagate reservation_id through router (eng-router)
- [ ] require reservation_id for toolcall responses (eng-runtime)
- [ ] billing: dedupe by reservation_id + terminal_nonce (billing)
- [ ] console: add reserved vs committed columns + fallback badge (console)
- [ ] add reconciler job to scan for stale reservations and emit credits (billing/infra)
ashley: I'll open PRs for the router + runtime changes and link to this thread.
samir: thanks. goal: no user sees >1 charge for a single logical request even if fallback/retry/toolcall/truncation happen. will follow up with a small design doc once PRs land.
